definitions.explanation: An exam given to students who failed the original exam, providing another opportunity to pass.

examples.japanese: {再試験|さいしけん}を{受|う}ける。
{試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちたので、{再試験|さいしけん}を{受|う}けることになった。
examples.english: I failed the exam, so I have to take a retake.

examples.japanese: {再試験|さいしけん}で{合格|ごうかく}しないと{単位|たんい}がもらえない。
examples.english: If I don't pass the retake exam, I won't get the credit.

notes:
Compound of {再|さい} (again) + {試験|しけん} (exam). Specifically for students who took but failed the original exam.

FORMS:
Commonly shortened to {再試|さいし} in student speech.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {再試験|さいしけん}を{受|う}ける: to take a retake exam
- {再試験|さいしけん}に{合格|ごうかく}する: to pass the retake
- {再試験|さいしけん}の{対象|たいしょう}: eligible for a retake

USAGE:
Some institutions cap the maximum grade on a retake (e.g., {可|か} or C only). The retake is typically harder or covers more material.

RELATED WORDS:
- {追試|ついし}: make-up exam (for students who were absent, not who failed)
- {補講|ほこう}: make-up class
- {単位|たんい}: academic credit
